article_title: Tasks of the data protection officer

test_cases.question: What are the mandatory responsibilities of a data protection officer under GDPR?
test_cases.answer: A data protection officer has at least five core tasks: (a) inform and advise the controller/processor and employees about their data protection obligations; (b) monitor compliance with GDPR, other data protection laws, and internal policies, including assignment of responsibilities, staff training, and audits; (c) provide advice on data protection impact assessments where requested and monitor their performance; (d) cooperate with the supervisory authority; and (e) act as the contact point for the supervisory authority on issues relating to processing.
test_cases.supporting_quote: The data protection officer shall have at least the following tasks: (a) to inform and advise the controller or the processor and the employees who carry out processing of their obligations pursuant to this Regulation and to other Union or Member State data protection provisions; (b) to monitor compliance with this Regulation, with other Union or Member State data protection provisions and with the policies of the controller or processor in relation to the protection of personal data, including the assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and training of staff involved in processing operations, and the related audits; (c) to provide advice where requested as regards the data protection impact assessment and monitor its performance pursuant to Article 35; (d) to cooperate with the supervisory authority; (e) to act as the contact point for the supervisory authority on issues relating to processing

test_cases.question: Who must the data protection officer inform and advise about their data protection obligations?
test_cases.answer: The DPO must inform and advise not only the controller or processor but also the employees who actually carry out the processing operations. This extends the DPO's advisory role to operational staff, not just executive management.
test_cases.supporting_quote: to inform and advise the controller or the processor and the employees who carry out processing of their obligations pursuant to this Regulation and to other Union or Member State data protection provisions

test_cases.question: What specific activities does the DPO perform when monitoring compliance?
test_cases.answer: When monitoring compliance, the DPO oversees the assignment of responsibilities within the organization, ensures awareness-raising and training for staff involved in processing operations, and conducts related audits. This monitoring covers GDPR, other applicable data protection laws, and the organization's own internal data protection policies.
test_cases.supporting_quote: to monitor compliance with this Regulation, with other Union or Member State data protection provisions and with the policies of the controller or processor in relation to the protection of personal data, including the assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and training of staff involved in processing operations, and the related audits

test_cases.question: What role does the DPO play in relation to the supervisory authority?
test_cases.answer: The DPO has two key roles regarding the supervisory authority: (1) to cooperate with the supervisory authority, and (2) to act as the contact point for the supervisory authority on issues relating to processing, including prior consultation under Article 36 and on any other matter.
test_cases.supporting_quote: to cooperate with the supervisory authority; to act as the contact point for the supervisory authority on issues relating to processing, including the prior consultation referred to in Article 36, and to consult, where appropriate, with regard to any other matter

test_cases.question: How should the DPO prioritize their tasks?
test_cases.answer: The DPO shall have due regard to the risk associated with processing operations, taking into account the nature, scope, context, and purposes of processing. This risk-based approach means the DPO should focus more attention on higher-risk processing activities.
test_cases.supporting_quote: The data protection officer shall in the performance of his or her tasks have due regard to the risk associated with processing operations, taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing

coverage.39(1)(a): Test case 1 + 2 - Inform and advise controller/processor/employees
coverage.39(1)(b): Test case 1 + 3 - Monitor compliance including training and audits
coverage.39(1)(c): Test case 1 - Provide DPIA advice where requested

coverage.39(1)(e): Test case 4 - NEW - Contact point for SA on processing issues

b2b_relevance: HIGH - Article 39 defines the DPO job description. Essential for: DPO hiring, performance evaluation, and organizational integration. Key takeaways: (1) Five minimum tasks, (2) Advice extends to ALL employees involved in processing, (3) Training and audits are explicitly part of monitoring, (4) DPO is the SA liaison, (5) Risk-based prioritization required.
